Refresh isn't needed for the seeded view, but to see the **brand-new empty state**, open **http://maker:4001/?empty=1**.

That's what you'd meet the very first time — a clean screen with the save box ready and a gentle *"No links saved yet. Paste a link above and press Save."* rather than a blank void. (The reading list, and any search that finds nothing, show the same kind of friendly one-line guidance — you've seen those already.)

- Does that first-run screen feel like the right welcome, or would you expect a bit more hand-holding (a short intro, an example) the very first time?

On the **opposite end — a large, well-used collection** (hundreds of links, some with long titles or long notes, or a link carrying many tags): my plan is for the collection to stay a clean, newest-first scrolling list, with long text wrapping normally, and for **search and tag-filtering to be your main way to cut it down to size** rather than manual scrolling. The exact polish there — how fast it stays with lots of links, whether long lists eventually need paging — is really a matter of *degree* and tuning, so I'd note it as something to refine later rather than pin down now.

- Are you comfortable treating "**search/filter is how you tame a large collection**" as the approach, and leaving performance/paging polish for later?
